title: The Millers move in: homeowners forms and Section I coverages
summary: Help Dana fit Rosa with the right HO form, then live through the Millers' first fall in their new house: Coverages A to D, special limits, trees.
objectives: Match each homeowners form to its perils basis and who it fits
Place a property loss under Coverage A, B, C or D
Apply the 2011 Coverage C special limits, including the theft-only limits
Recall the tree, tree removal and ordinance or law additional coverages

scenes.title: The Millers move in: which homeowners form?
scenes.subtitle: HO forms, Coverages A to D, special limits, trees (2011 ISO HO forms; HO-2, HO-5, HO-8 from the 2000 forms)

beats.text: October in Grand Rapids. The Millers just got the keys to their new house. Dana picks their homeowners form.
beats.say: October in Grand Rapids. The Millers just got the keys to their new house. Dana picks their homeowners form.

beats.text: There's more than one?
beats.say: There's more than one?

beats.text: Six, actually. Homeowners is 15% of your exam: 22 items. Amounts are from the 2011 forms unless another edition is named; the 2022 forms changed some. For HO-2, HO-5 and HO-8, we use the 2000 edition.
beats.say: Six, actually. Homeowners is fifteen percent of your exam: twenty two items. Amounts are from the twenty eleven forms unless another edition is named; the twenty twenty two forms changed some. For H O two, H O five and H O eight, we use the two thousand edition.

scenes.title: Named perils vs open perils
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils A–B; HO 00 02 10 00; confusion pair cp_personal-06; memory hook mn_prop-10
scenes.plain: Named perils: only the causes the policy lists are covered. Open perils: every cause is covered unless the policy excludes it.
scenes.example: A party. Named perils is a guest list: not on it, no entry. Open perils is a banned list: everyone else gets in.
scenes.exam: Watch out: open doesn't mean everything. The exclusions, like flood, still apply.

beats.text: Named perils: only the causes listed are covered. Open perils: every cause is covered, unless excluded.
beats.say: Named perils: only the causes listed are covered. Open perils: every cause is covered, unless excluded.

beats.text: At a party, named perils is a guest list: not on it, no entry. Open perils is a banned list: everyone else gets in.
beats.say: At a party, named perils is a guest list: not on it, no entry. Open perils is a banned list: everyone else gets in.

beats.text: Watch out: open isn't everything. Exclusions, like flood, still apply.
beats.say: Watch out: open isn't everything. Exclusions, like flood, still apply.

scenes.title: Three forms for owners who live there
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 02 10 00 and HO 00 05 10 00 (2000), HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils; AIC 43 (eligibility); cp_personal-10

draw.text: For the owner-occupant of a 1 to 4 family home
Open on: A, B and C

beats.text: Owners living in their 1 to 4 family home, like the Millers, start with three forms.
beats.say: Owners living in their one to four family home, like the Millers, start with three forms.

beats.text: HO-2, the Broad Form: 16 named perils on the house, other structures and belongings. Those are Coverages A, B and C.
beats.say: H O two, the Broad Form: sixteen named perils on the house, other structures and belongings. Those are Coverages A, B and C.

beats.text: HO-3, the Special Form: open perils on the house and other structures. Belongings get those same 16 named perils, including theft.
beats.say: H O three, the Special Form: open perils on the house and other structures. Belongings get those same sixteen named perils, including theft.

beats.text: HO-5, the Comprehensive Form: open perils on all three.
beats.say: H O five, the Comprehensive Form: open perils on all three.

scenes.title: HO-2, HO-3 or HO-5?
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 02 10 00 and HO 00 05 10 00 (2000), HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils; cp_personal-10 drills; question prop-gap-09

cards.text: Sam spills a can of paint on the hardwood floor. It isn't a named peril, so this form won't pay for the floor.
cards.why: Of these three forms, only HO-2 covers the house for named perils. HO-3 and HO-5 cover the house on open perils.

cards.text: Jen wants the house, the shed and everything inside covered for any direct physical loss not excluded.
cards.why: HO-5 is open perils on Coverages A, B and C.

cards.text: The house is covered unless excluded. Jen's ring slips off at the lake, no sign of theft: not paid.
cards.why: HO-3: open perils on A and B, but 16 named perils on C. Losing a ring isn't one of them.

cards.text: The weight of ice and snow cracks the roof. It's paid only because that peril is on the house's list of 16.
cards.why: Of these three forms, only HO-2 names its perils for the house. Weight of ice, snow or sleet is one of its 16.

cards.text: A diamond ring slips off at the lake and is lost. No theft, yet this form can cover it.
cards.why: Under the 2000 HO-5, belongings get open perils, so a lost ring can be covered, up to its jewelry limit. Losing isn't named in HO-2 or HO-3.

beats.text: Your turn. Count the open coverages: HO-2, HO-3 or HO-5?
beats.say: Your turn. Count the open coverages: H O two, H O three or H O five?

reveal.text: HO-2: all named. HO-3: open house, named belongings. HO-5: all open.
reveal.say: H O two: all named. H O three: open house, named belongings. H O five: all open.

scenes.title: A number for every form
scenes.src: Adapted from memory hook mn_prop-13; AIC 43; ISO HO 00 04 05 11; HO 00 06 05 11, Cov. A; HO 00 08 10 00, Peril 9
scenes.hook: 2: Broad, a named list. 3: Special, the house is open. 4: the four walls aren't yours. 5: high five, all open. 6: the condo unit. 8: eight-track, older homes.
items: HO-4, tenants: Coverages C and D only, no A or B
HO-6, condo owners and co-op shareholders: A covers alterations, appliances, fixtures, improvements
HO-8 (2000 edition): older homes; 10 named perils; theft on premises only, up to $1,000 per loss

beats.text: Number peg: 2 Broad, a named list. 3 Special, the house is open. 4, renters: the four walls aren't yours, so only Coverages C and D, no A or B. 5, high five: open on everything. 6, the condo unit. 8, the eight-track: older homes.
beats.say: Number peg: two Broad, a named list. Three Special, the house is open. Four, renters: the four walls aren't yours, so only Coverages C and D, no A or B. Five, high five: open on everything. Six, the condo unit. Eight, the eight track: older homes.

beats.text: Rosa's grandma owns a condo in Traverse City. HO-6 is for condo owners and co-op shareholders. Its Coverage A covers her unit's alterations, appliances, fixtures and improvements, not the whole building.
beats.say: Rosa's grandma owns a condo in Traverse City. H O six is for condo owners and co-op shareholders. Its Coverage A covers her unit's alterations, appliances, fixtures and improvements, not the whole building.

beats.text: HO-8, from the 2000 edition, fits older homes whose replacement cost far exceeds market value. It covers 10 named perils. Theft: on the premises only, up to $1,000 per loss.
beats.say: H O eight, from the two thousand edition, fits older homes whose replacement cost far exceeds market value. It covers ten named perils. Theft: on the premises only, up to one thousand dollars per loss.

scenes.title: Dana's call: a form for Rosa
scenes.src: AIC 43 (ISO 2011 HO program eligibility); ISO HO 00 04 05 11, Sec. I; question prop-gap-10

draw.text: I rent. Just cover my stuff!

beats.text: Next at Dana's desk: Rosa, the Millers' tenant in Lansing.
beats.say: Next at Dana's desk: Rosa, the Millers' tenant in Lansing.

beats.text: Just cover my stuff! Which form, Dana?
beats.say: Just cover my stuff! Which form, Dana?

options.label: An HO-3, like a homeowner's
options.fail: HO-2, HO-3, HO-5 and HO-8 may be issued only to the owner-occupant of a 1 to 4 family dwelling. Rosa rents.

beats.text: I don't own this house!
beats.say: I don't own this house!

beats.text: Not eligible: HO-3 needs an owner who lives there.
beats.say: Not eligible: H O three needs an owner who lives there.

options.label: An HO-6, like Grandma's
options.fail: HO-6 is for condo unit owners and co-op shareholders, not tenants.

beats.text: HO-6 is for condo unit owners and co-op shareholders, like Grandma. Rosa just rents.
beats.say: H O six is for condo unit owners and co-op shareholders, like Grandma. Rosa just rents.

draw.text: For condo unit owners and co-op shareholders
I don't own a unit. I rent!

options.label: An HO-4
options.win: HO-4 is for tenants: Coverage C for belongings, Coverage D for loss of use, and no Coverage A or B.

beats.text: HO-4 it is: Coverage C for your belongings, and D for loss of use.
beats.say: H O four it is: Coverage C for your belongings, and D for loss of use.

reveal.text: HO-4: C and D only. The four walls aren't hers.
reveal.say: H O four: C and D only. The four walls aren't hers.

scenes.title: The Millers' 2011 HO-3, letter by letter
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Coverages A, B, C.1–C.2; question prop-gap-12, prop-gap-13; memory hook mn_prop-14

draw.text: A: the house, attached structures, repair materials on site
C: belongings, anywhere in the world
Other home or self-storage: 10% of C or $1,000, whichever is greater

beats.text: The Millers get a 2011 HO-3. Coverage A: the house, attached structures like their garage, and repair materials on site.
beats.say: The Millers get a twenty eleven H O three. Coverage A: the house, attached structures like their garage, and repair materials on site.

beats.text: Coverage B: other structures, set apart by clear space, like the shed. 10% of A, and using it doesn't reduce A.
beats.say: Coverage B: other structures, set apart by clear space, like the shed. Ten percent of A, and using it doesn't reduce A.

beats.text: Coverage C: their belongings, anywhere in the world. Jen's bike stolen outside her office? Covered.
beats.say: Coverage C: their belongings, anywhere in the world. Jen's bike stolen outside her office? Covered.

beats.text: Things usually kept at another home of theirs, or in self-storage: 10% of C or $1,000, whichever is greater.
beats.say: Things usually kept at another home of theirs, or in self-storage: ten percent of C or one thousand dollars, whichever is greater.

beats.text: The land itself? Not covered.
beats.say: The land itself? Not covered.

scenes.title: Which coverage pays?
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Coverages A.1, B.1, C.1; Perils B.7, B.9; questions prop-gap-12, prop-gap-13

items.why: A structure attached to the house is part of the dwelling: Coverage A.

items.text: Fire burns the backyard tool shed
items.why: Set apart from the house by clear space: an other structure, Coverage B.

items.text: A burglar takes the Millers' TV
items.why: The TV is a belonging: Coverage C. Theft is one of its named perils.

items.text: Lumber stacked by the house for porch repairs burns
items.why: Materials and supplies on or next to the premises, for repairing the dwelling, are Coverage A.
A garage set apart by clear space is an other structure: Coverage B.

items.text: Smoke from a kitchen fire stains the couch
items.why: The couch is a belonging: Coverage C. Smoke is one of its named perils.

beats.text: Your turn: which coverage pays?
beats.say: Your turn: which coverage pays?

reveal.text: Attached is A, set apart is B, belongings are C.
reveal.say: Attached is A, set apart is B, belongings are C.

scenes.title: Forced out of the house: Coverage D
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Coverage D.1–3; confusion pair cp_personal-07; question prop-044
scenes.plain: Pays the extra cost of living elsewhere after a covered loss, plus the fair rental value of any part you rent out.
scenes.example: A covered fire guts the Millers' kitchen. While it's rebuilt, their hotel and restaurant bills above their normal costs go to D.
scenes.exam: One limit for all of D. Civil authority bars you from home over covered damage next door: up to 2 weeks.

beats.text: Coverage D, loss of use. It pays the extra cost of living elsewhere after a covered loss. Say a covered fire wrecks the Millers' kitchen.
beats.say: Coverage D, loss of use. It pays the extra cost of living elsewhere after a covered loss. Say a covered fire wrecks the Millers' kitchen.

beats.text: While it's rebuilt, D pays additional living expense: hotel and restaurant bills above normal. The same limit covers fair rental value, if part is rented out.
beats.say: While it's rebuilt, D pays additional living expense: hotel and restaurant bills above normal. The same limit covers fair rental value, if part is rented out.

beats.text: Say a covered fire next door, and the city bars the Millers from their home. Civil authority: up to 2 weeks. One limit covers all of D.
beats.say: Say a covered fire next door, and the city bars the Millers from their home. Civil authority: up to two weeks. One limit covers all of D.

scenes.q: The Millers' 2011 HO-3 has $60,000 of Coverage C. Sam keeps $9,000 of gear (its actual cash value) in a self-storage unit. A covered fire destroys it. Ignoring the deductible, the policy pays:
scenes.why: Property in self-storage, or usually kept at another residence, is limited to 10% of C or $1,000, whichever is greater. 10% of $60,000 is $6,000.

beats.text: Quick check: Sam's $9,000 of gear burns in a storage fire. What's paid?
beats.say: Quick check: Sam's nine thousand dollars of gear burns in a storage fire. What's paid?

reveal.text: $6,000: self-storage gets 10% of C or $1,000, whichever is greater.
reveal.say: Six thousand dollars: self-storage gets ten percent of C or one thousand dollars, whichever is greater.

scenes.title: Special limits: a walk through the house
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Coverage C.3.a–i; adapted from memory hook mn_prop-16

beats.text: Under the 2011 HO-3, some belongings get their own cap per loss: special limits. Let's tour the house.
beats.say: Under the twenty eleven H O three, some belongings get their own cap per loss: special limits. Let's tour the house.

beats.text: Kitchen cookie jar, cash: $200. Hall desk: securities, deeds, passports and tickets, $1,500. Garage: boat, trailer and motor, same.
beats.say: Kitchen cookie jar, cash: two hundred dollars. Hall desk: securities, deeds, passports and tickets, one thousand five hundred dollars. Garage: boat, trailer and motor, same.

beats.text: Now the trap. Bedroom jewelry box: $1,500 for jewelry, watches and furs, but that cap is for theft only. Firearms in the basement gun safe, and the dining-room silverware: $2,500 each, also theft only.
beats.say: Now the trap. Bedroom jewelry box: one thousand five hundred dollars for jewelry, watches and furs, but that cap is for theft only. Firearms in the basement gun safe, and the dining-room silverware: two thousand five hundred dollars each, also theft only.

beats.text: Home office: $2,500 of business property at home, $1,500 away. None of these adds to Coverage C.
beats.say: Home office: two thousand five hundred dollars of business property at home, one thousand five hundred dollars away. None of these adds to Coverage C.

scenes.title: Sam's call: the Thanksgiving burglary
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Perils B.9 (theft); Coverage C.3.a, C.3.e; question prop-041

draw.text: Stolen: $4,000 necklace and $500 cash. 2011 HO-3, Coverage C: $60,000

beats.text: Thanksgiving: a burglar breaks in, taking Jen's necklace, worth $4,000, and $500 cash. It's their 2011 HO-3; forget the deductible. What should Sam do?
beats.say: Thanksgiving: a burglar breaks in, taking Jen's necklace, worth four thousand dollars, and five hundred dollars cash. It's their twenty eleven H O three; forget the deductible. What should Sam do?

options.label: File and expect all $4,500 back
options.fail: Each special limit is the most paid per loss for that kind of property: theft of jewelry $1,500, money $200.

beats.text: The check: $1,700. Special limits cap jewelry theft and cash.
beats.say: The check: one thousand seven hundred dollars. Special limits cap jewelry theft and cash.

options.label: Skip the claim: burglary isn't covered
options.fail: Theft is one of the HO-3's 16 named perils for personal property. Sam should file.

beats.text: Sam never files. Theft is a named peril.
beats.say: Sam never files. Theft is a named peril.

beats.text: Sam! That's money on the table.
beats.say: Sam! That's money on the table.

options.label: File, and expect $1,700
options.win: Theft of jewelry, watches and furs: $1,500 per loss. Money: $200 per loss. $1,700 in all, before the deductible.

beats.text: Right: $1,500 for the jewelry, $200 for the cash.
beats.say: Right: one thousand five hundred dollars for the jewelry, two hundred dollars for the cash.

reveal.text: Special limits are per loss, and they don't add to Coverage C.
reveal.say: Special limits are per loss, and they don't add to Coverage C.

scenes.q: Rewind: no burglar. Under the 2011 HO-3, a kitchen fire destroys Jen's necklace, actual cash value $4,000. Coverage C is $60,000. Ignoring the deductible, the policy pays:
scenes.why: The $1,500 jewelry limit applies only to loss by theft. A fire loss is paid in full, within the Coverage C limit.

beats.text: Rewind. No burglar: a kitchen fire destroys the necklace. What's paid?
beats.say: Rewind. No burglar: a kitchen fire destroys the necklace. What's paid?

reveal.text: $4,000. Fire isn't theft, so the jewelry limit doesn't apply.
reveal.say: Four thousand dollars. Fire isn't theft, so the jewelry limit doesn't apply.

scenes.title: Additional coverages: yard and code (2011 HO-3)
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Additional Coverages E.1.b, E.3, E.11; questions prop-045, prop-046; memory hook mn_prop-17

draw.text: Must damage a covered structure or block a driveway or handicap ramp
Extra cost of rebuilding to code after a covered loss

beats.text: Now the yard, under the 2011 HO-3. Its additional coverages include trees, shrubs and plants: up to 5% of A, $500 per tree.
beats.say: Now the yard, under the twenty eleven H O three. Its additional coverages include trees, shrubs and plants: up to five percent of A, five hundred dollars per tree.

beats.text: Their perils include theft and vandalism, but not windstorm.
beats.say: Their perils include theft and vandalism, but not windstorm.

beats.text: Watch out: tree removal, another additional coverage, is different. It pays to remove trees felled by windstorm, hail, or weight of ice, snow or sleet. Up to $1,000 per loss, $500 per tree.
beats.say: Watch out: tree removal, another additional coverage, is different. It pays to remove trees felled by windstorm, hail, or weight of ice, snow or sleet. Up to one thousand dollars per loss, five hundred dollars per tree.

beats.text: But only if they damage a covered structure or block a driveway or handicap ramp.
beats.say: But only if they damage a covered structure or block a driveway or handicap ramp.

beats.text: Ordinance or law is also an additional coverage. After a covered fire, the city may require rebuilding to today's code. Up to 10% of A pays the extra cost, as additional insurance.
beats.say: Ordinance or law is also an additional coverage. After a covered fire, the city may require rebuilding to today's code. Up to ten percent of A pays the extra cost, as additional insurance.

scenes.title: Sam's call: the maple in the driveway
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. I Additional Coverages E.1.b (tree removal) and E.3 (trees); question prop-045

beats.text: December. A windstorm drops the Millers' healthy maple across the driveway. Their car can't get out. What should Sam claim?
beats.say: December. A windstorm drops the Millers' healthy maple across the driveway. Their car can't get out. What should Sam claim?

options.label: A new maple, under the trees coverage
options.fail: Trees, shrubs and plants are covered for fire, lightning, theft, vandalism and a few others, but not windstorm.

beats.text: Denied. Windstorm isn't a tree peril. No new maple.
beats.say: Denied. Windstorm isn't a tree peril. No new maple.

options.label: Skip it: wind-blown trees get nothing
options.fail: Tree removal pays to remove a windstorm tree that blocks a driveway: up to $500 per tree, $1,000 per loss.

beats.text: Sam spends a weekend sawing, for nothing. Removal would have paid, up to $500.
beats.say: Sam spends a weekend sawing, for nothing. Removal would have paid, up to five hundred dollars.

options.label: Claim tree removal: the car is blocked in
options.win: Tree removal: up to $1,000 per loss, $500 per tree, for a windstorm-felled tree that blocks a driveway or damages a covered structure.

beats.text: Approved: it blocks the driveway. Removal pays up to $500 for this tree.
beats.say: Approved: it blocks the driveway. Removal pays up to five hundred dollars for this tree.

reveal.text: Wind-felled trees aren't replaced. Removal pays only if one damages a covered structure or blocks a driveway or handicap ramp.
reveal.say: Wind-felled trees aren't replaced. Removal pays only if one damages a covered structure or blocks a driveway or handicap ramp.

items: HO-2 named; HO-3 open on A and B; HO-5 open on A, B and C
HO-4: C and D only. HO-6 A: unit fixtures, not the building
Attached structures are A; detached are B, at 10% of A
HO-3: jewelry, firearms and silverware limits are theft only
HO-3 trees: 5% of A, not windstorm. Ordinance or law: 10% of A

beats.text: What a fall! HO-2 is all named perils. HO-3 is open on A and B, and HO-5 on A, B and C. Renters get the HO-4: C and D only. In an HO-6, Coverage A covers the unit's fixtures, not the building.
beats.say: What a fall! H O two is all named perils. H O three is open on A and B, and H O five on A, B and C. Renters get the H O four: C and D only. In an H O six, Coverage A covers the unit's fixtures, not the building.

beats.text: Attached structures are A; detached ones are B, at 10% of A. HO-3 jewelry, firearms and silverware limits are theft only. HO-3 trees: up to 5% of A, but not for windstorm. Ordinance or law: up to 10% of A.
beats.say: Attached structures are A; detached ones are B, at ten percent of A. H O three jewelry, firearms and silverware limits are theft only. H O three trees: up to five percent of A, but not for windstorm. Ordinance or law: up to ten percent of A.

beats.say: Next up: winter. How bad can it be?

clipsay.s9.why: Property in self-storage, or usually kept at another residence, is limited to ten percent of C or one thousand dollars, whichever is greater. Ten percent of sixty thousand dollars is six thousand dollars.
clipsay.s11.o0.fail: Each special limit is the most paid per loss for that kind of property: theft of jewelry, one thousand five hundred dollars; money, two hundred dollars.
